t: Love on the Cross
v: It was now about the sixth hour, and darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour.
The sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was torn in two.
Jesus, crying with a loud voice, said, “Father, into your hands I commit my spirit!” Having said this, he breathed his last.
When the centurion saw what was done, he glorified God, saying, “Certainly this was a righteous man.”
All the multitudes that came together to see this, when they saw the things that were done, returned home beating their chests.
All his acquaintances and the women who followed with him from Galilee stood at a distance, watching these things.
b: These were the final moments of Jesus on the cross. As he breathed his last, darkness covered the land and the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom. This was more than a natural event; it was God declaring something great to the world: because of Jesus’ sacrifice, the wall separating people from God has been torn down.

In Old Testament times, the veil separated the Most Holy Place from everything outside, showing that sinners could not come freely into the presence of a holy God. But when Jesus shed his blood and gave his life on the cross, he himself became the way, so that everyone who believes in him may come boldly to the Father. The cross is not a defeat; it is salvation completed.

Before he died, Jesus said, “Father, into your hands I commit my spirit.” Even in his most painful hour, he trusted the Father completely. He did not only die for us; he also left us an example of faith. When we meet darkness and suffering in life, we too can place ourselves in the Father’s hands, as Jesus did.

The centurion saw all this and could not help but confess, “Certainly this was a righteous man.” The love of the cross moved the people of that day, and it has moved countless hearts through every generation. For the cross shows us that God is not distant and far above us; he came among us himself and bore the price of our sin. This is the greatest love in the world, and a grace that never changes.
a: Give Thanks for the Lord’s Salvation
Often reflect on the price Jesus paid for us.
Come Boldly to God
Because of Christ, we can draw near to the Father.
Learn a Life of Entrusting
In every circumstance, place yourself in God’s hands.
q: When I think of Jesus being crucified for me, does this love still move my heart?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for sending Jesus to die on the cross for my sins. Because of his sacrifice, I am reconciled to You and can come into Your presence. Help me to remember this salvation often, to no longer live for myself but for the Lord who loves me. Teach me, in every day of my life, to learn to place myself completely in Your hands. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Because of the salvation of the cross, I can come boldly to the Father.

t: Fear God and Turn from Sin
v: “Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy.
You shall labor six days, and do all your work,

but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God. You shall not do any work in it, you, nor your son, nor your daughter, your male servant, nor your female servant, nor your livestock, nor your stranger who is within your gates;
“Honor your father and your mother, that your days may be long in the land which the LORD your God gives you.
“You shall not murder.
“You shall not commit adultery.
“You shall not steal.
“You shall not give false testimony against your neighbor.
“You shall not covet your neighbor’s house. You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, nor his male servant, nor his female servant, nor his ox, nor his donkey, nor anything that is your neighbor’s.”
Moses said to the people, “Don’t be afraid, for God has come to test you, and that his fear may be before you, that you won’t sin.”
The people stayed at a distance, and Moses came near to the thick darkness where God was.
b: The Ten Commandments are not shackles God uses to restrict people; they are a standard for life that God has given. Just as a train must run on its tracks to reach its destination safely, our lives must run according to God’s principles to live out true freedom and blessing. Apart from God’s truth, life may look free, but it easily leads to confusion and harm.

This passage speaks especially of rest, honoring parents, honesty, purity, and contentment. These commandments are not merely outward rules; they reflect a person’s inner life. Much sin does not begin on the outside but in the heart. Covetousness, if left unaddressed, may turn into stealing; selfish desire, if not dealt with, can lead to an even greater fall. So God looks not only at our actions but at our hearts.

Moses said, “God has come… that his fear may be before you, that you won’t sin.” To fear God is not to be afraid of his punishment; it is to know his holiness, love, and glory, and so to be willing to honor him as great. When people lose the fear of God, they easily become self-centered; when they fear God, they seek his will in everything.

Today’s world stresses that people may do as they please, but God reminds us that a truly blessed life does not follow our own desires; it obeys God’s truth. When we let God be Lord of our lives, fearing and obeying him, we can escape the snares of sin and live a life of peace and joy.
a: Honor God’s Word
Let God’s truth be the standard for your life.
Guard Your Heart
Watch for covetousness and selfish desire within.
Learn to Fear God
Center everything on God and follow his will.
q: In what matters do I act only by my own will without seeking God’s heart?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for giving us Your truth as the way for our lives. Help me not only to know Your Word but to be willing to obey it. Keep my heart from sin and temptation, and let me always hold a reverent fear of You. May I live each day in Your will and bring glory to Your name. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will fear God, obey the truth, and live a blessed life.

t: Lord, Guard My Heart and My Mouth
v: LORD, I have called on you. Come to me quickly! Listen to my voice when I call to you.
Let my prayer be set before you like incense; the lifting up of my hands like the evening sacrifice.
Set a watch, LORD, before my mouth. Keep the door of my lips.
Don’t incline my heart to any evil thing, to practice deeds of wickedness with men who work iniquity. Don’t let me eat of their delicacies.
Let the righteous strike me, it is kindness; let him reprove me, it is like oil on the head; don’t let my head refuse it; Yet my prayer is always against evil deeds.
For my eyes are on you, LORD, the Lord. I take refuge in you. Don’t leave my soul destitute.
Keep me from the snare which they have laid for me, from the traps of the workers of iniquity.
Let the wicked fall together into their own nets while I pass by.
b: When David faced attacks from his enemies and all kinds of temptation, his first prayer was not for God to change his circumstances, but for God to guard his heart and his mouth. He knew deeply that enemies on the outside may be frightening, but a deviation on the inside is far more dangerous. One word that should not be spoken, one wrong thought, often does more harm than an external difficulty.

So David prayed, “Set a guard, Yahweh, before my mouth. Keep the door of my lips.” The tongue is small, yet it can have enormous effect. A word of encouragement can build up a life; a hurtful word can leave lasting scars. A wise person does not only ask God to change others, but first asks God to govern his own mouth.

David also asked God not to incline his heart to evil. He knew that sin seldom happens suddenly; it begins in the heart and slowly drifts away. When people begin to envy the way of the wicked and enjoy the benefits of sin, they easily move step by step away from God. So true victory is not only refusing temptation from outside, but guarding the heart within.

Most remarkable of all, David was willing to accept rebuke from the righteous. He saw rebuke as healing oil, not as humiliation. A humble person is willing to be reminded and corrected, and so keeps growing. When we fix our eyes on God and accept his light and guidance, we can avoid the enemy’s snares and walk on the right path of life.
a: Ask God to Govern Your Mouth
Speak words that build up, not words that hurt.
Guard Your Heart
Do not let sin and selfish desire take root in your heart.
Keep a Teachable Attitude
Be willing to receive reminders and correction.
q: Lately, have my words and thoughts glorified God and built up others?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, please guard my mouth, and guard my heart. Do not let me speak words that hurt others, and do not let my heart incline toward evil. Give me a humble, teachable spirit, willing to receive Your light and Your reminders. Help me to fix my eyes on You every day, to be freed from the enemy’s snares, and to walk on the path that pleases You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will fix my eyes on God, and ask the Lord to guard my heart and my mouth.

t: Put On the New Self, Live Out Christ
v: Don’t lie to one another, seeing that you have put off the old man with his doings,
and have put on the new man, who is being renewed in knowledge after the image of his Creator,
where there can’t be Greek and Jew, circumcision and uncircumcision, barbarian, Scythian, bondservant, or free person; but Christ is all, and in all.
Put on therefore, as God’s chosen ones, holy and beloved, a heart of compassion, kindness, lowliness, humility, and perseverance;
bearing with one another, and forgiving each other, if any man has a complaint against any; even as Christ forgave you, so you also do.
Above all these things, walk in love, which is the bond of perfection.
And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to which also you were called in one body, and be thankful.
b: Paul tells believers that trusting in the Lord is not merely changing one’s religious identity, but putting on the new self and living a new life. The old self is centered on itself, full of lies, pride, selfishness, and strife; the new self is continually renewed in Christ, more and more restoring the image in which God first created us.

This change is not a change of outward appearance, but of what is within. Paul compares it to changing clothes: we take off the deeds of the old self and put on a new character. Compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience are not something we force out by our own effort, but a life that flows naturally when Christ reigns within us.

Paul especially mentions bearing with one another and forgiving one another. The greatest challenge in the church and in the family is often not tasks but relationships. When people hold on to themselves and cling to others’ faults, walls arise; but when we think of how the Lord forgave us, we have strength to forgive others. Forgiveness does not deny the hurt; it hands judgment over to God and keeps love.

Finally, Paul points out that love is the bond of perfection, and that the peace of Christ must rule in our hearts. When Jesus becomes the center of life, love replaces coldness, peace overcomes strife, and thankfulness replaces complaining. This is the new life God delights in, and the most beautiful testimony a Christian can have.
a: Take Off the Old Self’s Life
Refuse lies, selfishness, and pride.
Put On Christ’s Character
Treat others with compassion, kindness, and humility.
Let Christ’s Peace Rule
Learn forgiveness and thankfulness in your relationships.
q: Is my life more like the old self now, or more and more like the new self that pleases Christ?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for giving me new life in Christ. Help me to put off the thoughts and actions of the old self, put on the new self, and live out Your image. Give me a heart of compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience, so that I can bear with and forgive others. May Your love fill me, and let the peace of Christ reign as King in my heart. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will put on the new self and let Christ’s love and peace reign in my life.

t: Come to the Lord Like a Little Child
v: They were bringing to him little children, that he should touch them, but the disciples rebuked those who were bringing them.
But when Jesus saw it, he was moved with indignation and said to them, “Allow the little children to come to me! Don’t forbid them, for God’s Kingdom belongs to such as these.
Most certainly I tell you, whoever will not receive God’s Kingdom like a little child, he will in no way enter into it.”
He took them in his arms and blessed them, laying his hands on them.
b: In those days children were generally thought unimportant, so the disciples tried to stop those who brought children to Jesus. But Jesus was indignant, because in his eyes every life is precious. He did not turn the children away; instead he took them in his arms himself and blessed them.

Jesus went on to say that the Kingdom of God belongs to such as these. He was not praising the childishness of children, but the simple, trusting heart of a child. A child knows their own limits and so is willing to depend on their parents; in the same way, anyone who wants to enter God’s Kingdom must admit their limits and trust the Father with all their heart.

Often, the older people grow, the more easily they rely on their own ability, knowledge, and experience. When all goes well, they feel they don’t need God; when trouble comes, they try to solve it by themselves. But what God delights in is a humble, dependent heart. True faith is not feeling very sure of ourselves, but believing that God is forever reliable.

Finally, Jesus took the children in his arms and blessed them. This shows us that God not only accepts us, but is glad to pour grace and blessing upon us. No matter how old we are, if we are willing to come to the Lord simply, like a child, we can experience his love and presence.
a: Believe God Simply
Depend on the Lord with a child’s faith.
Admit Your Limits
Do not rely on yourself, but depend on God.
Draw Near to Jesus
Come to the Lord each day to receive his love and blessing.
q: Am I relying on my own ability, or trusting God simply like a child?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for loving me and accepting me, embracing me as Jesus embraced the little children. Give me a simple, trusting heart that does not rely on my own cleverness and ability, but looks to You with all my heart. Help me to draw near to You always and live in Your love and blessing. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will trust God simply like a little child and live in his love and blessing.

t: The God Who Daily Bears Our Burdens
v: Let God arise! Let his enemies be scattered! Let them who hate him also flee before him.
As smoke is driven away, so drive them away. As wax melts before the fire, so let the wicked perish at the presence of God.
But let the righteous be glad. Let them rejoice before God. Yes, let them rejoice with gladness.
Sing to God! Sing praises to his name! Extol him who rides on the clouds: to the LORD, his name! Rejoice before him!
Blessed be the Lord, who daily bears our burdens, even the God who is our salvation. Selah.
God is to us a God of deliverance. To GOD, the Lord, belongs escape from death.
Sing to God, you kingdoms of the earth! Sing praises to the Lord—Selah—
to him who rides on the heaven of heavens, which are of old; behold, he utters his voice, a mighty voice.
Ascribe strength to God! His excellency is over Israel, his strength is in the skies.
You are awesome, God, in your sanctuaries. The God of Israel gives strength and power to his people. Praise be to God!
b: In this psalm David praises God as a victorious king. When God arises, his enemies are scattered and darkness retreats, like smoke driven away by the wind, like wax melting before fire. This is not because God is struggling with them, but because no power that opposes God can overcome his might and glory.

Yet this great God is not only the King who rules the universe; he is also the Father who daily bears our burdens. Verse 19 is a precious promise: “the Lord, who daily bears our burdens.” God does not help us only now and then; he walks with us every day. He knows our pressure, our worries, our tears, and our struggles, and he is willing to carry for himself the burdens we cannot bear.

David also declares, “God is to us a God of deliverances.” God’s rescue is not only entering eternal life in the future; it is his grace at work in everyday life. He can deliver us from sin, fear, despair, and every kind of bondage. Whatever difficulty we face, God is still the God who brings deliverance.

So David calls all the nations to sing to God and ascribe strength to him. When we fix our eyes on circumstances, we see how limited we are; when we fix our eyes on God, we see his limitless power. The God who gives strength and power to his people is still at work in our lives today. He not only bears our burdens, but gives us strength to keep moving forward.
a: Hand Your Burdens to God
Believe that God is willing to bear your burdens daily.
Remember God’s Salvation
Often count God’s grace and help.
Respond with Praise
Give glory and thanks to him.
q: What is the heaviest load I carry lately? Am I truly willing to entrust it to God?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that You are not only the Almighty God but also the Lord who daily bears my burdens. When I feel weary and under pressure, help me place everything in Your hands. Thank You that You are the God of deliverance and the One who gives strength to Your people. May I no longer focus on my own limits, but fix my eyes on Your great power and faithfulness. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: God bears my burdens every day, and he will give me strength to go forward with courage.

t: Be the Salt and Light of the World
v: “You are the salt of the earth, but if the salt has lost its flavor, with what will it be salted? It is then good for nothing, but to be cast out and trodden under the feet of men.
“You are the light of the world. A city located on a hill can’t be hidden.
Neither do you light a lamp and put it under a measuring basket, but on a stand; and it shines to all who are in the house.
Even so, let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven.
b: Jesus told his disciples, “You are the salt of the earth, and the light of the world.” He did not say you will become salt and light someday, but that you already are. When Christ lives in us, our lives carry the mission of influencing the world.

Salt prevents decay and adds flavor. In a world full of selfishness, indifference, and sin, Christians should live out honesty, goodness, and love, and bring a positive influence. If believers’ lives are no different from the world’s, they are like salt that has lost its flavor, having lost the testimony they should have.

Light drives away darkness and shows the way. Darkness does not need to be chased out; when light appears, darkness retreats on its own. In the same way, God does not want us to complain about the darkness, but to become light. When we live out Christ’s life, showing love at home, integrity at work, and hope among people, we shine God’s light out.

Jesus especially reminds us that light is not for displaying ourselves, but for glorifying the Father. A life that truly belongs to God does not lift itself up, but lets people see God’s grace and work through us. When people see our good works and give glory to the Father, we are living out the mission of salt and light.
a: Live Out the Influence of Salt
Influence those around you with love and truth.
Live Out the Testimony of Light
Reveal Christ in dark surroundings.
Glorify God Alone
Let people see God, not lift yourself up.
q: Is my life influencing the people around me to draw closer to God?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for choosing me to be the salt and light of the world. Help me to live out Christ’s life each day, neither compromising with the world nor hiding Your light. May my words, attitudes, and actions all glorify You, so that more people come to know You and turn to You through my testimony. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will live as salt and light, and give the glory to the Father.

t: Keep the Faith
v: I command you therefore before God and the Lord Jesus Christ, who will judge the living and the dead at his appearing and his Kingdom:
preach the word; be urgent in season and out of season; reprove, rebuke, and exhort with all patience and teaching.
For the time will come when they will not listen to the sound doctrine, but having itching ears, will heap up for themselves teachers after their own lusts,
and will turn away their ears from the truth, and turn away to fables.
But you be sober in all things, suffer hardship, do the work of an evangelist, and fulfill your ministry.
For I am already being offered, and the time of my departure has come.
I have fought the good fight. I have finished the course. I have kept the faith.
From now on, the crown of righteousness is stored up for me, which the Lord, the righteous judge, will give to me on that day; and not to me only, but also to all those who have loved his appearing.
b: These are words the apostle Paul wrote in the last stage of his life, and his deepest charge to Timothy. He knew the time of his departure was near, so he entrusted the most important thing to his spiritual son: preach the word, and faithfully proclaim God’s truth.

Paul foretold that many would not like sound doctrine and would not want to listen to God’s word, wanting only to hear what they like. Our generation is the same; people often seek messages that please them, satisfy them, and flatter them, but are unwilling to face the light of truth and be changed. But a servant of God must not cater to people; he must be faithful to God’s commission.

So Paul urged Timothy, “Be sober in all things, suffer hardship, fulfill your ministry.” The road of following the Lord is not always easy, but faithfulness matters more than success. What God values is not how great our achievements are, but whether we are faithful to complete the mission he has entrusted to us.

Finally, Paul said with satisfaction and hope, “I have fought the good fight. I have finished the course. I have kept the faith.” What is most precious in life is not how much wealth or fame we have, but that on the day we see the Lord, we can say with confidence, “Lord, I have faithfully walked the road you gave me.” Then the crown of righteousness will be our eternal reward.
a: Hold Faithfully to the Truth
Do not stray from God’s way when circumstances change.
Fulfill Your Duty
Be faithful to the end in the place God has put you.
Fix Your Eyes on the Eternal Reward
Live for the Lord, not only for this life.
q: If I were to see the Lord today, could I say as Paul did, “I have kept the faith”?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for entrusting truth and mission to me. Give me faithfulness and courage, that I may not follow the currents of the world but hold fast to Your word. Help me to fulfill my duty in daily life and ministry, and follow You to the end in good times and bad. When I see You face to face, may I too say with joy that I have finished the course and kept the faith. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will follow the Lord faithfully, keep the faith, and finish the course God has entrusted to me.

t: Don’t Give the Devil a Foothold
v: “Be angry, and don’t sin.” Don’t let the sun go down on your wrath,
and don’t give place to the devil.
Let him who stole steal no more; but rather let him labor, producing with his hands something that is good, that he may have something to give to him who has need.
Let no corrupt speech proceed out of your mouth, but only what is good for building others up as the need may be, that it may give grace to those who hear.
Don’t grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.
Let all bitterness, wrath, anger, outcry, and slander be put away from you, with all malice.
And be kind to one another, tender hearted, forgiving each other, just as God also in Christ forgave you.
b: Paul reminds believers that spiritual warfare does not happen only at special moments, but in everyday life. When people hold on to anger for a long time, refuse to forgive, and let bitterness stay in their hearts, they give the devil room to work. So Paul says, “Don’t let the sun go down on your wrath, and don’t give place to the devil.”

Anger itself is not necessarily sin, but if we let it ferment, it may turn into resentment, revenge, and harm. Many broken relationships come not from a single conflict but from unwillingness to deal with the anger in the heart. God wants us to bring the problem to the Lord, rather than let anger take root within.

Paul also stresses the importance of words. Corrupt, hurtful, judgmental words tear people down, while words that build up bring healing and encouragement. When Christ reigns in us, our mouth is no longer a tool for wounding but a channel for blessing. For as the life is, so are the words.

Finally, Paul turns the focus to forgiveness. God has forgiven us in Christ, so we also must forgive others. True victory is not winning an argument, but overcoming bitterness with love; not insisting that we are right, but letting Christ’s grace flow through our lives. When we treat others with kindness, compassion, and forgiveness, we live out the likeness of Christ.
a: Deal with Anger Promptly
Do not let bitterness build up in your heart.
Speak Words That Build Up
Let your words be a source of blessing to others.
Learn to Forgive Others
Because God has forgiven us first.
q: Is there still bitterness, anger, or someone I am unwilling to forgive in my heart?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, please search my heart and remove all bitterness, resentment, and anger. Help me not to give the devil a foothold, but to let the Holy Spirit reign within me. Teach me to treat others with kindness and compassion, and give me strength to forgive, just as You forgave me in Christ. May my words and my life become a blessing to others. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will live in kindness and forgiveness, and give the devil no foothold.

t: He Bore Everything for Us
v: Who has believed our message? To whom has the LORD’s arm been revealed?
For he grew up before him as a tender plant, and as a root out of dry ground. He has no good looks or majesty. When we see him, there is no beauty that we should desire him.
He was despised and rejected by men, a man of suffering and acquainted with disease. He was despised as one from whom men hide their face; and we didn’t respect him.
Surely he has borne our sickness and carried our suffering; yet we considered him plagued, struck by God, and afflicted.
But he was pierced for our transgressions. He was crushed for our iniquities. The punishment that brought our peace was on him; and by his wounds we are healed.
All we like sheep have gone astray. Everyone has turned to his own way; and the LORD has laid on him the iniquity of us all.
He was oppressed, yet when he was afflicted he didn’t open his mouth. As a lamb that is led to the slaughter, and as a sheep that before its shearers is silent, so he didn’t open his mouth.
b: More than seven hundred years before Jesus was born, Isaiah prophesied of this suffering servant. When he came into the world, he had no dazzling appearance and no illustrious position; instead he was despised, rejected, and cast off. Yet the one people looked down on was exactly the Savior God prepared for all humanity.

The most moving thing in this passage is the repeated words “for us.” He was pierced for our transgressions and crushed for our iniquities; he bore our sickness and carried our suffering. The punishment that should have fallen on us fell on Jesus; the debt of sin we should have repaid, he paid in full.

The Bible says, “All we like sheep have gone astray. Everyone has turned to his own way.” The root of sin is not only doing wrong, but leaving God and going our own way. Our greatest problem is not our circumstances, but the “self” within that always wants to be in charge. Jesus came to bring lost sheep back to the Father’s arms, to reconcile people to God again.

When Jesus faced humiliation, flogging, and the cross, he did not defend himself or strike back. Like a lamb he silently bore it all, because he knew this was the way of redemption. The cross shows us God’s justice, and it also shows us God’s love. However weak or failing we are today, if we come to the Lord we can receive forgiveness, peace, and new life.
a: Give Thanks for the Lord’s Atonement
Often reflect on the price Jesus paid for us.
Turn Back to God
No longer go your own way, but follow the Lord’s way.
Receive the Lord’s Healing
Hand your guilt, burdens, and wounds to Jesus.
q: When I think of Jesus suffering for me and giving his life for me, am I willing to give him authority over my life?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for sending Jesus into the world, pierced for my sins and crushed for my transgressions. Thank You that he bore my sorrows and carried my suffering, so that I can receive forgiveness, peace, and new life. Help me no longer to go my own way, but to follow You every day. May I remember the grace of the cross all my life and give all the glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Jesus has borne everything for me. I will trust him, follow him, and live in his grace.

t: Move Forward, and God Will Fight for You
v: When Pharaoh came near, the children of Israel lifted up their eyes, and behold, the Egyptians were marching after them; and they were very afraid. The children of Israel cried out to the LORD.
They said to Moses, “Because there were no graves in Egypt, have you taken us away to die in the wilderness? Why have you treated us this way, to bring us out of Egypt?

Isn’t this the word that we spoke to you in Egypt, saying, ‘Leave us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians’? For it would have been better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in the wilderness.”
Moses said to the people, “Don’t be afraid. Stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD, which he will work for you today; for you will never again see the Egyptians whom you have seen today.
The LORD will fight for you, and you shall be still.”
The LORD said to Moses, “Why do you cry to me? Speak to the children of Israel, that they go forward.
Lift up your rod, and stretch out your hand over the sea and divide it. Then the children of Israel shall go into the middle of the sea on dry ground.
Behold, I myself will harden the hearts of the Egyptians, and they will go in after them. I will get myself honor over Pharaoh, and over all his armies, over his chariots, and over his horsemen.
The Egyptians shall know that I am the LORD when I have gotten myself honor over Pharaoh, over his chariots, and over his horsemen.”
b: Not long after the Israelites left Egypt, they faced a desperate situation: the Red Sea ahead and the pursuing army behind. When they saw Pharaoh’s army drawing near, their hearts were full of fear, and they even regretted leaving Egypt. In a crisis, people easily see only their circumstances and forget God’s past grace and deeds.

But Moses spoke words full of faith to the people: “Don’t be afraid. Stand still, and see the salvation of Yahweh, which he will work for you today.” True faith does not deny difficulty; it believes in the midst of difficulty that God is in control. When people see the Red Sea, they see an obstacle; when God sees the Red Sea, he sees an opportunity to reveal his glory.

Then God said, “Yahweh will fight for you.” Often we think everything must be solved by our own effort, when real victory comes from God. Some battles in life are won not by might nor by power, but by God’s Spirit. When we are willing to hand authority over to God, we can experience his wonderful works.

But God did not say only “stand still”; he also said “go forward.” Faith is not waiting in place; it is advancing boldly on God’s promise. Before the waters parted, the Israelites had to believe God first; before the way was clear, they had to take the first step. God is saying to us today as well: don’t keep looking at the Red Sea, don’t keep looking at the pursuers, but go forward in faith, for God will fight for you.
a: Don’t Be Frightened by Circumstances
Fix your eyes on God, not on the problem.
Believe God Is at Work
Place what you cannot solve in God’s hands.
Move Forward in Faith
Obey God’s leading and do not stay stuck in fear.
q: What is the “Red Sea” in my life right now? Is God calling me to move forward in faith?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, when I face difficulty and the unknown, please remove my fear and unbelief. Help me to see not only the Red Sea before me but Your great power and faithfulness. Thank You for promising to fight for me, and for giving me courage to keep going forward. May I learn in every challenge to trust You, obey You, and follow You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will move forward in faith, for God will fight for me.

t: Grace of Restoration After Judgment
v: Though they dig into Sheol, there my hand will take them; and though they climb up to heaven, there I will bring them down.

Though they hide themselves in the top of Carmel, I will search and take them out from there; and though they be hidden from my sight in the bottom of the sea, there I will command the serpent, and it will bite them.
Though they go into captivity before their enemies, there I will command the sword, and it will kill them. I will set my eyes on them for evil, and not for good.
In that day I will raise up the tent of David who is fallen and close up its breaches, and I will raise up its ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old,
that they may possess the remnant of Edom and all the nations who are called by my name,” says the LORD who does this.

I will bring my people Israel back from captivity, and they will rebuild the ruined cities, and inhabit them; and they will plant vineyards, and drink wine from them. They shall also make gardens, and eat their fruit.
I will plant them on their land, and they will no more be plucked up out of their land which I have given them,” says the LORD your God.
b: Most of the message of Amos is judgment. Israel had abandoned God, oppressed the poor, and worshiped idols, thinking they could hide from God’s sight. But God declared that no matter where people hide, they cannot escape his eyes. God is a just God, and he does not overlook evil.

Yet the book of Amos does not end with judgment; it ends with hope. Right after the darkest message, God says, “I will raise up the tent of David who is fallen.” This shows that God’s heart is not only to tear down but to rebuild; not only to discipline but to restore. God allows brokenness to happen in order to bring deeper renewal.

The fallen tent of David symbolizes the glory and relationship with God that his people lost. God promises to close up the breaches himself and rebuild what has fallen. Today, whether it is a broken life, a wounded family, a cold faith, or even a failed ministry, if people are willing to turn back to God, he still has the power to build again.

Finally, God promises to bring the captives back, to plant again, build again, and be blessed again. This shows us that God’s grace is always greater than human failure. Perhaps life has seasons of desolation, but God does not want us to remain forever in the ruins. When we return to him, he can turn wasteland into vineyard, tears into laughter, and loss into blessing.
a: Revere God’s Justice
Do not take sin lightly, and do not hide from God’s searching light.
Believe God Can Rebuild
Hand the breaches in your life to the Lord to repair.
Hold On to God’s Promise
Believe God can make desolate land bear fruit again.
q: Are there places in my life that need God’s rebuilding and restoration?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that You are not only a just God but also a God full of grace and mercy. When I see my weakness and failure, help me to turn back to You. Please mend the breaches in my life and rebuild what has fallen, that I may experience Your grace and blessing again. Thank You that You can turn desolation into abundance and despair into hope. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: God will rebuild the breaches in my life, and make the desolate land blossom and bear fruit again.

t: As He Had Done Before
v: Then this Daniel was distinguished above the presidents and the local governors, because an excellent spirit was in him; and the king thought to set him over the whole realm.

Then the presidents and the local governors sought to find occasion against Daniel as touching the kingdom; but they could find no occasion or fault, because he was faithful. There wasn’t any error or fault found in him.
Then these men said, “We won’t find any occasion against this Daniel, unless we find it against him concerning the law of his God.”
Then these presidents and local governors assembled together to the king, and said this to him, “King Darius, live forever!

All the presidents of the kingdom, the deputies and the local governors, the counselors and the governors, have consulted together to establish a royal statute and to make a strong decree, that whoever asks a petition of any god or man for thirty days, except of you, O king, he shall be cast into the den of lions.
Now, O king, establish the decree and sign the writing, that it not be changed, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which doesn’t alter.”
Therefore King Darius signed the writing and the decree.

When Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house (now his windows were open in his room toward Jerusalem) and he kneeled on his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did before.
Then these men assembled together, and found Daniel making petition and supplication before his God.
b: Daniel was promoted in a foreign empire not because of political skill, but because he had “an excellent spirit.” His life held the character of honesty, faithfulness, and the fear of God, so that when his enemies tried to find fault with him, they could find no error or fault.

In the end, his enemies discovered that Daniel’s greatest trait was his faithfulness to God. They knew that if they could find nothing wrong in his work, character, or conduct, they could only attack his faith. So they set a trap, forbidding anyone to pray to God, hoping to get rid of him.

The most moving line is in verse 10: “as he did before.” Daniel knew the decree had been signed and that it might cost him his life, yet he did not panic, did not compromise, and did not secretly stop praying. He came before God just as he always had. True faith is not worshiping God only in good times, but staying faithful under pressure.

Many people only start looking for God when crisis comes, but Daniel could stand firm at the lions’ den because he had long since built a solid life of prayer. Faithfulness in ordinary days creates faith in times of danger. When circumstances changed, his habit did not change; when the world shook, his relationship with God did not shake.
a: Build a Steady Devotional Life
Draw near to God at a fixed time every day, not only pray when you have a need.
Be Faithful in Small Things
Let your character be the most powerful testimony.
Hold to Your Faith Under Pressure
Even at a cost, choose to follow the Lord faithfully.
q: When facing pressure and challenge, can I still draw near to God “as I did before,” as Daniel did?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for teaching me the lesson of faithfulness through Daniel’s life. Help me build a solid life of prayer, drawing near to You steadily in ordinary days. When I face pressure, temptation, and difficulty, give me courage and faith, so that I do not compromise or draw back, but keep following You faithfully. May my life also be a good testimony that glorifies Your name. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: However circumstances change, I will follow God faithfully, as I have done before.

t: Draw Near to God, and He Will Draw Near to You
v: Where do wars and fightings among you come from? Don’t they come from your pleasures that war in your members?
You lust, and don’t have. You murder and covet, and can’t obtain. You fight and make war. You don’t have, because you don’t ask.
You ask, and don’t receive, because you ask with wrong motives, so that you may spend it on your pleasures.
You adulterers and adulteresses, don’t you know that friendship with the world is hostility toward God? Whoever therefore wants to be a friend of the world makes himself an enemy of God.
Or do you think that the Scripture says in vain, “The Spirit who lives in us yearns jealously”?
But he gives more grace. Therefore it says, “God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”
Be subject therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners. Purify your hearts, you double-minded.
Lament, mourn, and weep. Let your laughter be turned to mourning and your joy to gloom.
Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he will exalt you.
b: James points out plainly that the root of many conflicts and quarrels between people is neither circumstances nor others, but selfish desire within. When people center on themselves, always wanting to get more, grasp more, and prove themselves more, envy, comparison, and rivalry follow. Outer problems often reflect the inner condition.

So God does not deal with the outer disputes first; he deals with the heart. James reminds us that the greatest danger is not outward difficulty, but a heart that gradually drifts from God and begins to befriend the world. When our eyes are fixed only on the world’s values, people’s praise, and our own interests, we easily lose our hunger for God.

Yet God has not given up on us. Verse 6 says, “But he gives more grace.” What a precious promise! However weak we are, as long as we are willing to turn back, God’s grace is always greater than our failure. The question is not whether God is willing to give grace, but whether we are willing to come before him humbly.

So James gives a path to victory: submit to God, resist the devil, draw near to God. When we lay down pride, admit our limits, and return to seek God, he draws near to us. The closer people come to God, the further they are from sin; the nearer to God, the more strength to overcome temptation. True revival always begins with humility and drawing near to God.
a: Examine Your Heart
Watch for envy, comparison, or self-centeredness.
Choose to Draw Near to God
Spend time each day in prayer, Bible reading, and seeking the Lord.
Learn Humble Submission
Let God reign as King in your life.
q: Lately, am I drawing closer to God, or closer to the world? What does my heart truly long for?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, please search my heart, that I may see the hidden pride, selfishness, and desire within. Thank You for giving more grace, so that I can come back before You again. Help me to submit to You, resist the enemy, and draw near to You every day. May my heart no longer be drawn by the world, but long for You alone. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will draw near to God, and God will draw near to me; I will humbly submit to the Lord and live in his grace.

t: Guard the Field God Has Entrusted
v: After him was Shammah the son of Agee, a Hararite. The Philistines had gathered together into a troop where there was a plot of ground full of lentils; and the people fled from the Philistines.
But he stood in the middle of the plot and defended it, and killed the Philistines; and the LORD worked a great victory.
b: This passage has only two short verses, yet it records a stirring story of victory. When the Philistine army attacked, everyone fled, leaving only Shammah standing alone in the field. From a human point of view it was a war with no chance of winning, but Shammah did not choose to run; he chose to stand.

It was only a field of lentils, seemingly of no special value. But to Shammah it was an inheritance God had given, a field God had entrusted. He knew that if everyone gave up, no one would be able to keep the blessing God had given. So he was willing to pay the price and stood faithfully at his post.

Often we face similar situations. When others draw back, are we still willing to hold to the truth? When circumstances are hard, are we still willing to serve faithfully? God does not necessarily call everyone to accomplish great and dramatic things, but he calls us to faithfully guard the field entrusted to us, which may be our family, workplace, church, small group, or the mission God has given us.

The passage ends: “Yahweh worked a great victory.” The victory came not because Shammah was strong, but because he was willing to stand, and God himself went to work. Often God is looking not for the most capable, but for the most willing to be faithful to the end. When people stand firm in their place, God’s power is revealed.
a: Don’t Despise What God Entrusts
Faithfully guard the responsibility God has given you.
Keep Standing in Difficulty
Do not draw back because circumstances are hard.
Believe God Gives Victory
Do your part faithfully and leave the result to God.
q: What is the “field” God has given me now? Am I guarding it, or running from it?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for entrusting me with different responsibilities and missions. Give me a faithful and courageous heart like Shammah’s, so that even if others draw back, I am still willing to stand; even if circumstances are hard, I still hold on. Help me faithfully guard all You have entrusted, believing that true victory comes from You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will faithfully guard the field God has entrusted to me, for Yahweh will give me victory.

t: Rest and the Origin of Life
v: The heavens, the earth, and all their vast array were finished.
On the seventh day God finished his work which he had done; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had done.
God blessed the seventh day, and made it holy, because he rested in it from all his work of creation which he had done.
This is the history of the generations of the heavens and of the earth when they were created, in the day that the LORD God made the earth and the heavens.
No plant of the field was yet on the earth, and no herb of the field had yet sprung up; for the LORD God had not caused it to rain on the earth. There was not a man to till the ground,
but a mist went up from the earth, and watered the whole surface of the ground.
The LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
b: Right at the start of Genesis 2, we see that God completed the great work of creation. God rested on the seventh day, not because he was weary, but because everything was finished. In this he established the principle of rest, reminding us that true satisfaction comes not from ceaseless work but from being with God.

Today’s world is full of busyness and pressure, and many think they must keep running to prove their worth. But God set apart the Sabbath as holy so that people would learn to stop and return to him. True rest is not only rest for the body; it is the soul returning to the Creator’s embrace, finding new strength in him.

Then the Bible describes the creation of man. God formed man’s body from the dust of the ground, and breathed the breath of life into his nostrils. This tells us that people are not merely physical beings, but living souls. Our worth lies not in wealth, ability, or position, but in being made according to God’s purpose and having life that comes from God.

So the greatest need in life is not only success at work or a comfortable living, but a relationship with the God who made us. When people leave God, they gradually wither like branches cut off from the vine; when they return to God, they find life’s true meaning, direction, and rest.
a: Learn to Rest in God
Do not only be busy with work, but also draw near to God.
Value Your Identity
Remember that you are created and loved by God.
Live Out Life’s Purpose
Walk with God and glorify the Lord who created you.
q: Is my life being consumed in ceaseless busyness, or am I finding true rest in God?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for creating me and giving me the breath of life. Help me not merely to be busy with life, but to know how to rest in You. Let me remember that my worth comes not from achievement but from my identity as one You love. May I walk with You every day and receive peace, strength, and direction for life in Your presence. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I am a person created by God, and I will find true rest and life in him.

t: God Will Supply All Your Needs
v: You yourselves also know, you Philippians, that in the beginning of the Good News, when I departed from Macedonia, no assembly shared with me in the matter of giving and receiving but you only.
For even in Thessalonica you sent once and again to my need.
Not that I seek for the gift, but I seek for the fruit that increases to your account.
But I have all things and abound. I am filled, having received from Epaphroditus the things that came from you, a sweet-smelling fragrance, an acceptable and well-pleasing sacrifice to God.
My God will supply every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
b: The church in Philippi was a church full of love and action. When Paul faced difficulties and needs in preaching the gospel, they did not stand by, but supplied his needs again and again. This giving was not only financial support; it was participation in God’s Kingdom work and care for God’s servant.

Paul stressed that what he valued was not the gift itself, but the fruit in the giver’s life. Every willing, joyful act of giving is not simply a loss, but spiritual wealth laid up before God. What God values is not the amount given, but the heart of love for God and for people behind it.

Paul even described these gifts as “a sweet-smelling fragrance,” a sacrifice pleasing to God. In the Old Testament, the fragrance of the sacrifice symbolized God’s acceptance of people’s worship. Today, when we willingly give our time, money, gifts, and loving service to the Lord, we too become a fragrant offering that pleases God.

So Paul declares a precious promise: “My God will supply every need of yours according to his riches in glory.” God does not promise to satisfy all our wants, but to supply our true needs. When we are willing to put God’s concerns first, he will also care for us according to his abundant grace. God’s supply never runs short, for he is the Lord of abundance.
a: Gladly Support God’s Work
Take part in the work of God’s Kingdom with love.
Learn to Give Willingly
Offer your time, gifts, and resources to God.
Trust God’s Provision
Entrust your needs to the faithful Father.
q: Am I willing to use the resources God has given me to be a blessing to others and a help to God’s Kingdom?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that You are the God of rich provision. Help me to have a generous heart, to care not only for my own needs but also for the needs of others and the work of Your Kingdom. Let me learn to manage faithfully all You have entrusted to me, believing that You will supply all I need according to Your riches in glory. May my life become a fragrant offering that You accept. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: My God will supply all my needs according to his riches in glory.

t: No Longer I, but Christ
v: For I through the law died to the law, that I might live to God.

I have been crucified with Christ, and it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me. That life which I now live in the flesh, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself up for me.
I don’t reject the grace of God. For if righteousness is through the law, then Christ died for nothing!”
b: This passage is the deepest confession of Paul’s life of faith and the heart of the gospel. Paul once tried hard to keep the law, hoping to please God by his own works, but he later understood that people cannot reach God’s standard by their own effort. The law lets people see their sin, but it cannot truly change a life.

So Paul says, “I have been crucified with Christ.” The cross is not only the death of Jesus; it also represents the end of the old self. That old life, centered on self, wanting to be justified by itself and to be master of its own life, has been crucified with Christ. The greatest purpose of God’s salvation is not only to forgive our sins, but to give us a new life.

Then Paul declares, “It is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me.” This does not mean Paul lost his personality, but that the ownership of his life changed. Before, self was in charge; now Christ is in charge. Before, he lived by himself; now he lives by Christ. A truly victorious life depends not on human willpower, but on letting Christ reign and work within us.

Finally, Paul puts all the focus on God’s grace. Salvation is not through human merit, but because Jesus loved us and gave himself for us. When we understand this love, we are willing to give ourselves to the Lord. The greatest freedom in life is not to live as we please, but to let Christ live out his life in us.
a: Lay Down Your Own Authority
Let Jesus be the true Master of your life.
Live by Christ
Do not rely on your own ability, but depend on the Lord’s grace.
Often Reflect on the Cross
Remember that Jesus loved me and gave himself for me.
q: In which areas of my life am I still in charge myself, rather than letting Christ reign?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for redeeming me through the cross of Jesus Christ. Help me to no longer live in self-centeredness, but to let Christ live in me. When I am weak, be my strength; when I am lost, be my direction. May I live in Your grace every day, so that people may see Christ in my life. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: No longer I, but Christ lives in me.

t: Filled with the Spirit, Living Out Christ
v: Now when the day of Pentecost had come, they were all with one accord in one place.
Suddenly there came from the sky a sound like the rushing of a mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting.
Tongues like fire appeared and were distributed to them, and one sat on each of them.
They were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak with other languages, as the Spirit gave them the ability to speak.
Now there were dwelling in Jerusalem Jews, devout men, from every nation under the sky.
When this sound was heard, the multitude came together and were bewildered, because everyone heard them speaking in his own language.
“Let all the house of Israel therefore know certainly that God has made him both Lord and Christ, this Jesus whom you crucified.”
Now when they heard this, they were cut to the heart, and said to Peter and the rest of the apostles, “Brothers, what shall we do?”
b: When the day of Pentecost came, the Holy Spirit came as Jesus had promised and filled all the disciples gathered there. Disciples who had been weak and timid received power through the Holy Spirit and began to witness boldly for the Lord. This shows us that God never wants us to accomplish his work by our own cleverness, talent, and strength, but to seek the leading of the Holy Spirit and let him work within us. True service turns from relying on ourselves to relying on the Holy Spirit.

The center of being filled with the Spirit is not displaying human gifts, but lifting up Jesus. Peter’s message finally focused on one sentence: “God has made him both Lord and Christ.” In a person truly filled with the Holy Spirit, the focus of life moves more and more from self to Jesus; they no longer insist on being their own master, but let Jesus reign within as King. When we yield to the Holy Spirit, Christ’s life can be lived out from within us, so that people not only hear us talk about Jesus, but see Jesus in us.

When Peter preached the gospel, the people “were cut to the heart.” What truly changes lives is not human eloquence, but the Holy Spirit shining through God’s word into people’s hearts, so that they see themselves, repent, and turn to God. So sharing the gospel is not showing how powerful we are, but letting the Holy Spirit use us to bring people to Jesus. We are only vessels; it is God who truly changes lives. So the result of service is not to glorify ourselves, but to give all the glory to Jesus.
a: Rely on the Holy Spirit
Seek the Holy Spirit’s guidance every day, and do not act on your own.
Let Jesus Be Lord
Hand the authority of your life to Christ and let him reign within.
Live Out Christ
Witness to Jesus by your life and words, and give the glory to God.
q: Am I living and serving by my own strength now, or relying on the Holy Spirit and letting Jesus be Lord within me?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for giving the Holy Spirit to dwell in me. Fill me with the Holy Spirit every day, so that I no longer rely on my own cleverness and ability but submit to Your leading. May Jesus reign as King in me, and may I live out Christ and witness to Christ, so that more people come to know Jesus through my life. All the glory be to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will be filled with the Holy Spirit, and let Jesus be Lord and King in my life.

t: God’s Great Power Revealed in Weakness
v: But we have this treasure in clay vessels, that the exceeding greatness of the power may be of God and not from ourselves.
We are pressed on every side, yet not crushed; perplexed, yet not to despair;
pursued, yet not forsaken; struck down, yet not destroyed;
always carrying in the body the putting to death of the Lord Jesus, that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our body.
For we who live are always delivered to death for Jesus’ sake, that the life also of Jesus may be revealed in our mortal flesh.
So then death works in us, but life in you.
But having the same spirit of faith, according to that which is written, “I believed, and therefore I spoke.” We also believe, and therefore we also speak,
knowing that he who raised the Lord Jesus will raise us also through Jesus, and will present us with you.
For all things are for your sakes, that the grace, being multiplied through the many, may cause the thanksgiving to abound to the glory of God.
Therefore we don’t faint, but though our outward person is decaying, yet our inward person is renewed day by day.
For our light affliction, which is for the moment, works for us more and more exceedingly an eternal weight of glory,
while we don’t look at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen. For the things which are seen are temporal, but the things which are not seen are eternal.
b: Paul compares us to “clay vessels”: limited, fragile, even breakable; yet inside the clay vessels is a treasure. God wants us to understand that true power is not from ourselves, but from him. When we no longer try to prove ourselves, but admit our limits and depend on the Holy Spirit, God’s great power is revealed all the more. The focus is not on how beautiful the vessel is, but on the treasure within; the focus of life is not on ourselves, but on Jesus.

Paul says, “always carrying in the body the putting to death of the Lord Jesus, that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our body.” This is the path of the cross-life: the old self laid down, Christ’s life lived out; no longer insisting on being our own master, but letting Jesus reign within. When we are willing to give up self and obey God, Christ’s love, humility, patience, and power can flow through us. It is not that I am so capable, but that the Lord does his work within me, and in the end all glory goes to God.

So Paul says, “We don’t faint.” He looked not only at what was before him, but at the present from the viewpoint of eternity. Circumstances change, bodies decay, and suffering comes, but Christ’s life can be renewed day by day. When we turn our eyes from ourselves, others, and circumstances to Jesus, we are no longer trapped by temporary difficulties, and can see God working eternal glory in our lives.
a: Admit Your Limits
Don’t struggle on by yourself; learn to depend on the Holy Spirit.
Let Jesus Live Within
Lay down self-rule and let Christ reign.
Fix Your Eyes on Eternity
Don’t be limited by present circumstances; look to Jesus with full attention.
q: In the difficulty I face now, am I struggling on by myself, or letting Jesus reign within me and reveal his power?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for putting the treasure in this limited clay vessel of mine. Help me no longer to rely on myself, but to depend on the Holy Spirit and let Jesus reign within me. Even in weakness and difficulty, keep me from losing heart; renew me day by day, so that I live out Christ’s life and all glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Though I am a clay vessel, God’s exceeding great power will be revealed in me.

t: God Wants Your Heart
v: Now, Israel, what does the LORD your God require of you, but to fear the LORD your God, to walk in all his ways, to love him, and to serve the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul,
to keep the LORD’s commandments and statutes, which I command you today for your good?
Behold, to the LORD your God belongs heaven, the heaven of heavens, and the earth, with all that is therein.
Only the LORD had a delight in your fathers to love them, and he chose their offspring after them, even you above all peoples, as it is today.
b: Just before the Israelites entered the Promised Land, Moses asked the most important question: “What does the LORD your God require of you?” The answer is not more religious ritual, but a heart that truly turns to God: to fear him, walk in his ways, love him, and serve him with all your heart and soul. True faith is not outward performance but an inner change of ownership. It is not running your own life and asking God to help now and then; it is letting God be God and letting him reign in your life.

Why does God deserve to be loved with all our heart? Because “to the LORD your God belong heaven and the heaven of heavens, the earth, with all that is therein.” He is Lord of all, yet he delights in loving his people. God does not ask us to serve him because he lacks something, but because he loved and chose us first. True service is not trading work for God’s love; it is gladly offering ourselves to him after we have been won by his love.

Everything God commands is ultimately “for your good.” So obedience is not the loss of freedom but entry into the abundance God has prepared. When we stop insisting on our own way, take God’s word as our standard, seek his guidance, and follow the life of Christ, we discover that giving our life to God is not losing ourselves but finding our true selves. What God wants is not only how much we do, but that our whole heart belongs to him.
a: Fear God
Honor the Lord every day and let God hold first place in your life.
Walk in God’s ways
Don’t only understand the truth; live out God’s word.
Serve God with all your heart
Not to gain glory for yourself, but to gladly offer your life to the Lord.
q: God wants my heart. Where in my life have I not yet fully given it to him?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for loving me and choosing me first. Give me a heart that fears You, so that I gladly walk in Your ways and love and serve You with all my heart and soul. Help me let go of my own rule and let You be King in my life, so that everything I do pleases You and all the glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will fear the LORD, walk in his ways, and love and serve him with all my heart and soul.

t: Fix Your Eyes on Jesus and Run to the End
v: Therefore let’s also, seeing we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, lay aside every weight and the sin which so easily entangles us, and let’s run with perseverance the race that is set before us,
looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising its shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
For consider him who has endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, that you don’t grow weary, fainting in your souls.
You have not yet resisted to blood, striving against sin.
You have forgotten the exhortation which reasons with you as with children, “My son, don’t take lightly the chastening of the Lord, nor faint when you are reproved by him;
for whom the Lord loves, he disciplines, and chastises every son whom he receives.”
It is for discipline that you endure. God deals with you as with children, for what son is there whom his father doesn’t discipline?
For they indeed for a few days disciplined us as seemed good to them, but he for our profit, that we may be partakers of his holiness.
Follow after peace with all men, and the sanctification without which no man will see the Lord,
b: The Christian life is like a long-distance race. To run far, we must lay aside our burdens and the sin that entangles us. Much of what wears us out is not only outside difficulty but the pride, worry, bitterness, and self-centeredness within. God calls us to lay these hindrances down, to stop being bound by ourselves, and to run with perseverance the course he has set before us.

What matters most in running is not constantly checking how well we are doing, nor watching how fast others are going, but “looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith.” Jesus himself endured the suffering of the cross and left us an example. When we turn our focus from ourselves, others, and circumstances to Jesus, and think about his love and his cross, we find fresh strength in weariness and keep going in discouragement. He is not only the example we follow; he is the power that enables us to finish the whole race.

Discipline along life’s road is not God’s rejection but the mark of a Father who loves his children. God uses discipline to prune us, so that we let go of what does not please him and live out more of the holiness of Christ. So don’t only ask, “Why is this happening to me?” Ask, “Lord, what do you want to change in me through this?” True maturity is letting God renew us from the inside out, so that we pursue holiness and peace with everyone, until we have finished the course God has entrusted to us.
a: Lay aside life’s burdens
Remove sin and everything that hinders your growth in life.
Fix your eyes on Jesus
Look away from yourself, others, and circumstances, and follow the Lord with steady eyes.
Accept God’s discipline
Learn to obey in every circumstance, and become more and more like Christ.
q: What burden is entangling me right now, keeping me from fixing my eyes on Jesus and running the road ahead?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, help me lay aside every burden and the sin that so easily entangles me, so that my eyes look to Jesus alone. When I am tired and discouraged, let me think of the cross and find strength again. When You discipline and prune me, give me a humble and obedient heart, so that my life becomes more and more like Christ and I run faithfully to the end. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will lay aside every weight and the sin that entangles me, fix my eyes on Jesus, and run with perseverance the race set before me.

t: Seeing God’s Hindrance in Your Circumstances
v: God’s anger burned because he went; and the LORD’s angel placed himself in the way as an adversary against him. Now he was riding on his donkey, and his two servants were with him.

The donkey saw the LORD’s angel standing in the way, with his sword drawn in his hand; and the donkey turned out of the path, and went into the field. Balaam struck the donkey, to turn her into the path.
The donkey saw the LORD’s angel, and she thrust herself to the wall, and crushed Balaam’s foot against the wall. He struck her again.
The LORD’s angel went further, and stood in a narrow place, where there was no way to turn either to the right hand or to the left.
The donkey saw the LORD’s angel, and she lay down under Balaam. Balaam’s anger burned, and he struck the donkey with his staff.
The LORD opened the mouth of the donkey, and she said to Balaam, “What have I done to you, that you have struck me these three times?”
Balaam said to the donkey, “Because you have mocked me, I wish there were a sword in my hand, for now I would have killed you.”
The donkey said to Balaam, “Am I not your donkey, on which you have ridden all your life long until today? Was I ever in the habit of doing so to you?” He said, “No.”
Then the LORD opened the eyes of Balaam, and he saw the LORD’s angel standing in the way, with his sword drawn in his hand; and he bowed his head, and fell on his face.
b: Balaam was set on going forward, yet he didn’t see the angel of God standing in his way; his donkey saw it first. When things didn’t go as he wanted, Balaam didn’t seek God first. Instead he grew angry again and again and beat the donkey. We often do the same: we see only “who is blocking me,” and never first ask, “Is God using this situation to warn me?” Some of what we think are obstacles may in fact be God’s protection.

Balaam’s biggest problem was not that his eyes couldn’t see, but that his heart was clouded by his own will. When people insist on their own direction, they easily treat warnings as obstacles, protection as a nuisance, and even vent their anger on others. True humility is being willing to set aside our own judgment and return to our rightful place as human beings, letting God be God. Instead of rushing to blame others, we quietly ask first, “Lord, what do you want me to see?”

Only when “the LORD opened the eyes of Balaam” did he see the true spiritual picture, and at once he bowed his head to the ground. What we need in life is not only a smooth road but eyes opened by God. When we are willing to stop in our tracks, take God’s word as our standard, and seek the Holy Spirit’s leading, we can move from a human point of view to God’s. We no longer see only the trouble before us, but God’s guidance in our circumstances.
a: Seek God first when you meet obstacles
Don’t rush to complain; first ask what God is reminding you of.
Don’t vent your anger on people
Deal with your own heart first, then deal with the matter.
Ask God to open your spiritual eyes
Move from your own point of view to God’s.
q: Could the thing that has been frustrating me lately be a reminder God wants me to see?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, forgive me for so often seeing only the problems of my circumstances and other people, without first seeking Your heart. Open my eyes so that I see Your warnings and Your guidance. Help me let go of my stubbornness, humbly obey You, and let You be Lord of my life, leading me on Your path. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Lord, open my eyes so that I see your leading.

t: Keeping Yourselves in the Love of God
v: But you, beloved, keep building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Spirit.
Keep yourselves in God’s love, looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ to eternal life.
On some have compassion, making a distinction,
and some save, snatching them out of the fire with fear, hating even the clothing stained by the flesh.
b: Jude was written in a crisis, when false teaching and moral confusion were creeping into the church. Yet Jude didn’t tell believers to busy themselves criticizing others. He told them first to build up their own lives: “building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Spirit.” In a confused generation, the most important thing is not to change others first, but to let God’s truth change us first; to take God’s word as our standard and pray in the power of the Holy Spirit, so that our life is firmly rooted in Christ.

Then Jude says, “Keep yourselves in God’s love, looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ.” This is not about gripping God by our own effort, but about continually living within the reach of his love, with our eyes fixed on Jesus. When the focus is on ourselves, we easily become proud or discouraged; when it is on others, we easily judge or compare; when it returns to Jesus, we can stand firm in his love and mercy and let him reign in our hearts.

Once our life is built up, we go on to help others. Have compassion on those who doubt; actively rescue those in danger; and toward those stained by sin, show love while keeping holy boundaries. True love neither condones sin nor condemns people. It loves and has mercy as Jesus did, without compromising with sin. First connect our own life to the Lord, then use the love of Christ to support, rescue, and build up the lives of others.
a: Build yourself up in truth
Let God’s word renew your life every day.
Pray in the Holy Spirit
Don’t rely on your own methods; seek the Holy Spirit’s leading.
Rescue others with love
Have compassion on the weak while holding to truth and holiness.
q: Am I first rooting myself in truth, relying on the Holy Spirit, and staying in God’s love before I try to help others?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, root me in the truth, help me pray in the Holy Spirit, and keep me always living in Your love. Help me fix my eyes on Jesus and not live or serve by my own strength. Give me a compassionate heart too, so that in truth and love I can support the weak and bring back those who are lost. All the glory is Yours. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will build myself up on my most holy faith, pray in the Holy Spirit, and keep myself in the love of God.

t: God Will Show You the Way to Go
v: For this, let everyone who is godly pray to you in a time when you may be found. Surely when the great waters overflow, they shall not reach to him.
You are my hiding place. You will preserve me from trouble. You will surround me with songs of deliverance. Selah.
I will instruct you and teach you in the way which you shall go. I will counsel you with my eye on you.
b: After experiencing the forgiveness of his sin, David understood something deeply: don’t wait until the floodwaters of life rise to think of God, but draw near to him “in a time when you may be found.” Prayer is not the last resort when we have nowhere else to turn; it should be the starting point of each day. When we are willing to set aside our own opinions and quietly come before God, we move from relying on ourselves to relying on him, and he becomes the true Lord of our life.

God not only protects us in the storm; he becomes our “hiding place.” A hiding place is not a guarantee of a life without trouble, but a refuge that is always reliable in the midst of trouble. When our focus is on circumstances, we easily become afraid; when it returns to Jesus, we know we are still in God’s hands. True peace is not that everything changes the way I want, but that whatever happens, I know God is with me.

Even more precious, God promises, “I will instruct you and teach you in the way which you shall go.” What matters most in life is not how clever we are, but that we walk the road God wants us to walk. When we take God’s word as our standard, seek the Holy Spirit’s leading, and fix our eyes on following Jesus, we move from our own point of view to God’s. God does not merely point out the direction from a distance; he keeps his “eye on you,” and personally guides us along the road ahead.
a: Seek God early
Don’t wait for problems before you pray; draw near to the Lord every day.
Make God your hiding place
In hard times, don’t look at circumstances; fix your eyes on Jesus.
Obey God’s guidance
Stop insisting on your own way, and seek the way God wants you to go.
q: As I face the road of my life now, am I deciding the direction by myself, or seeking God’s guidance in prayer?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for being my hiding place and the God who guides my way. Help me draw near to You every day, not relying on my own cleverness but seeking the leading of the Holy Spirit. Whatever my circumstances, help me fix my eyes on Jesus, obey Your guidance, and walk the road You have prepared for me. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: God will instruct me and teach me the way I should go; he will counsel me with his eye on me.

t: Walking Together Requires One Heart
v: Only let your way of life be worthy of the Good News of Christ, that whether I come and see you or am absent, I may hear of your state, that you stand firm in one spirit, with one soul striving for the faith of the Good News;
If therefore there is any exhortation in Christ, if any consolation of love, if any fellowship of the Spirit, if any tender mercies and compassion,
make my joy full by being like-minded, having the same love, being of one accord, of one mind;
doing nothing through rivalry or through conceit, but in humility, each counting others better than himself;
each of you not just looking to his own things, but each of you also to the things of others.
b: Paul urged the church at Philippi to “stand firm in one spirit, with one soul striving for the faith of the Good News.” True unity doesn’t mean everyone’s personality and views are identical; it means everyone shares one center, Jesus Christ. When each person wants to go his own way, a team easily splits. When everyone turns their focus to Jesus and lets him be King, we can work together in our differences and move forward together for the gospel.

The greatest enemy of unity is often not lack of ability but a self that is too big. Rivalry, vain conceit, and competing over who matters more all come from self-centeredness. Paul shows the way to unity: “in humility, each counting others better than himself.” Humility is not denying our own worth; it is letting go of the need to grasp power, position, and face, and returning to the place God has given us. When we stop striving to prove ourselves, we can truly appreciate others and help them flourish.

So Paul says, “each of you not just looking to his own things, but each of you also to the things of others.” The life of Christ doesn’t only ask, “What do I want?” but begins to see what others need. True oneness is not held together by systems; it begins in life. First Christ changes me, then we build relationships of mutual love, and finally unity in ministry can arise. When each person is willing to let go of self and look out for one another, the church becomes a beautiful witness of the body of Christ.
a: Center on Jesus
When opinions differ, first seek the Lord’s heart.
Be humble
Prove yourself less; appreciate and build up others more.
Look out for one another
Don’t only look at your own needs; take the initiative to care for others.
q: In my family, church, or team, am I insisting on my own way, or humbly seeking one heart together?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, help me let go of self-centeredness and not crave glory for myself, but let Jesus be King in me.
