Give me a humble heart, so that I know how to appreciate, build up, and care for others, and walk together in unity with my brothers and sisters, striving as one for the gospel, so that all the glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will have a humble heart, looking not only to my own interests but also to the interests of others.

t: Don’t Let Busyness Make You Miss God’s Invitation
v: When one of those who sat at the table with him heard these things, he said to him, “Blessed is he who will feast in God’s Kingdom!”
But he said to him, “A certain man made a great supper, and he invited many people.
He sent out his servant at supper time to tell those who were invited, ‘Come, for everything is ready now.’
They all as one began to make excuses. “The first said to him, ‘I have bought a field, and I must go and see it. Please have me excused.’
“Another said, ‘I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I must go try them out. Please have me excused.’
“Another said, ‘I have married a wife, and therefore I can’t come.’

“That servant came, and told his lord these things. Then the master of the house, being angry, said to his servant, ‘Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in the poor, maimed, blind, and lame.’
“The servant said, ‘Lord, it is done as you commanded, and there is still room.’
“The lord said to the servant, ‘Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.
For I tell you that none of those men who were invited will taste of my supper. For many are called, but few are chosen.’”
b: Jesus uses a “great supper” as a picture of God’s invitation to salvation in his Kingdom. The host has prepared everything, and simply tells the guests, “Come, for everything is ready now.” Salvation is not earned by human effort; it is grace that God has already prepared and completed in Christ. The real question is not whether God has invited us, but whether we are willing to respond. The greatest blessing a person can have is to set aside his own arrangements, accept God’s invitation, and enter the abundant life God has prepared.

What is sobering is that those who refused were not off committing sins; they were busy with a field, oxen, and a family. None of these things is wrong in itself. The problem was “wrong order”: good things took the place of the most important thing. Today we too may be busy with work, family, and even ministry, so busy that we have no time to draw near to God. When our own plans matter more than God’s will, we are still sitting on the throne of our life. A true disciple lets Jesus come first, and in every choice asks first, “Lord, what would you have me do?”

The master then told his servant to go out and bring in the poor, maimed, blind, and lame, and even to invite more people from the highways and hedges. This shows that God’s grace is open to everyone, and that God longs for his house to be full. Those who have received grace must not enjoy the feast alone; they must go out and invite others in. When we truly experience Christ’s love, we begin to see the needs of the people around us, care for them with love, and bring them to Jesus, so that more people can share in the salvation God has prepared.
a: Put God first
Don’t let busyness replace your relationship with God.
Respond to God immediately
When you hear God’s call, obey and follow.
Invite people to Jesus
Take the initiative to care for those around you and share the grace of the gospel.
q: What “good thing” today is becoming my excuse for not responding to God and drawing near to him?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for preparing a rich salvation for me in Christ. Keep me from being so filled with busyness and my own plans that I miss Your invitation. Help me put Jesus first in my life and gladly obey Your will, and let me go out among people with Your love, inviting more to come to Jesus. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: The Lord has prepared everything for me. I will respond to his invitation and enter his abundant feast.

t: Walk with the Wise and Become Wise
v: Poverty and shame come to him who refuses discipline, but he who heeds correction shall be honored.
Longing fulfilled is sweet to the soul, but fools detest turning from evil.
One who walks with wise men grows wise, but a companion of fools suffers harm.
Misfortune pursues sinners, but prosperity rewards the righteous.
A good man leaves an inheritance to his children’s children, but the wealth of the sinner is stored for the righteous.
b: True wisdom shows itself first in whether we are willing to accept discipline. The proud take correction as an attack, but the humble take it as a chance to grow. When others point out our problems, what matters most is not to defend ourselves at once over “who is right and who is wrong,” but to return to God and ask, “Lord, what do I need to change?” Only those who are willing to see their own problems and be corrected by truth can keep maturing in life.

Wisdom is also closely tied to whom we choose to walk with. “One who walks with wise men grows wise.” People influence one another in relationships, and the longer we walk together, the more alike our values, thinking, and way of life become. So we need to walk with people who fear God, love the Lord humbly, and are willing to live out the truth, reminding, supporting, and building one another up, so that we not only know the truth but live it out.

True wisdom always bears the fruit of life in the end. The blessing of the righteous doesn’t stop with themselves; it becomes an inheritance for the next generation. That inheritance is not only money; far more precious are a life that fears God, an upright character, loving relationships, and an example of faith. The greatest success in life is not how much we own, but that after we leave this world we still leave behind a life whose influence brings others closer to God.
a: Humbly accept correction
When reproved, examine yourself first and don’t rush to defend yourself.
Choose wise companions
Build one another up with people who fear God and pursue truth.
Leave a legacy of life
Pass on faith, character, and love to the next generation.
q: Are the people I often walk with making me wiser and more like Christ?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, give me a humble, teachable heart, so that I am willing to accept reminders and correction. Place wise people who fear You in my life, so that we support and build one another up and follow Jesus together. May my life be not only blessed but also leave a godly inheritance, a blessing to many and to the next generation. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will walk with the wise, so that I become wise.

t: Night Passes, and Joy Comes in the Morning
v: I will extol you, LORD, for you have raised me up, and have not made my foes to rejoice over me.
LORD my God, I cried to you, and you have healed me.
LORD, you have brought up my soul from Sheol. You have kept me alive, that I should not go down to the pit.
Sing praise to the LORD, you saints of his. Give thanks to his holy name.
For his anger is but for a moment. His favor is for a lifetime. Weeping may stay for the night, but joy comes in the morning.
As for me, I said in my prosperity, “I shall never be moved.”
You, LORD, when you favored me, made my mountain stand strong; but when you hid your face, I was troubled.
I cried to you, LORD. I made supplication to the Lord:
“What profit is there in my destruction, if I go down to the pit? Shall the dust praise you? Shall it declare your truth?
Hear, LORD, and have mercy on me. LORD, be my helper.”
You have turned my mourning into dancing for me. You have removed my sackcloth, and clothed me with gladness,
to the end that my heart may sing praise to you, and not be silent. LORD my God, I will give thanks to you forever!
b: Looking back on his life, David saw that he had once fallen under the shadow of sickness, danger, and death; but when he cried out to God, God healed him, rescued him, and raised him up again. So he declared, “Weeping may stay for the night, but joy comes in the morning.” Trusting God doesn’t mean life will never have a dark night; it means knowing the night is not the end. Circumstances change and feelings change, but God’s favor lasts “for a lifetime.” So don’t let your focus stay on the night before you; turn it to the God who rules the morning.

Yet David also honestly admitted that when life was smooth he said, “I shall never be moved.” In good times people easily and unknowingly rely on themselves, mistaking God’s grace for their own ability. Only when God hid his face did David discover that what truly held him up was not himself but God’s grace. The real turning point in life is moving from “I can” back to “God can”: laying down our own sovereignty, letting God be God, and letting Jesus be King in our life.

In the end, David experienced God turning his “mourning into dancing” and exchanging his “sackcloth” for “gladness.” God doesn’t only bring us out of hardship; he uses hardship to change our lives, so that we come to know him more deeply through sorrow. Yesterday’s tears can become today’s testimony, and past pain can become comfort for others. When God restores our life, our best response is not to exalt ourselves but to give thanks to him without ceasing and give all the glory to God.
a: Look to God even in the night
Believe that hardship is not the final chapter of your life.
Rely on God even in good times
Don’t stand on your own strength; see everything as God’s grace.
Turn your experiences into testimony
Use God’s grace to comfort others and glorify God.
q: Am I willing to hand over the “night” I am going through to God, believing he can still turn my mourning into joy?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for being the God who shows favor all my life. Even when I am in the night, help me keep looking to You; and in good times, keep me from relying on myself. May You turn my mourning into dancing and my sorrow into joy, so that my life becomes a testimony of Your grace, and I give thanks to You all my days and give all the glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Weeping may stay for the night, but joy comes in the morning.

t: Trials Make Life Mature
v: Count it all joy, my brothers, when you fall into various temptations,
knowing that the testing of your faith produces endurance.
Let endurance have its perfect work, that you may be perfect and complete, lacking in nothing.
But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all liberally and without reproach, and it will be given to him.
But let him ask in faith, without any doubting, for he who doubts is like a wave of the sea, driven by the wind and tossed.
For that man shouldn’t think that he will receive anything from the Lord.
He is a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways.
Let the brother in humble circumstances glory in his high position;
and the rich, in that he is made humble, because like the flower in the grass, he will pass away.
For the sun arises with the scorching wind and withers the grass; and the flower in it falls, and the beauty of its appearance perishes. So the rich man will also fade away in his pursuits.
Blessed is a person who endures temptation, for when he has been approved, he will receive the crown of life which the Lord promised to those who love him.
b: James is not saying that trials are pleasant in themselves, but that we should see the work God is accomplishing behind them. Faith is like gold: it must be refined by fire to show its true worth. Trials also teach us endurance, so that our lives are gradually made “perfect and complete.” So when difficulty comes, don’t only ask, “Why me?” Ask, “Lord, how do you want to change my life through this?” When our viewpoint shifts from circumstances to God, a trial can turn from a stumbling block into a stepping stone for growth.

In trials, what we need most is not always an immediate change of circumstances but wisdom from God. James says, “If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God.” Human wisdom often just wants to escape the trouble quickly, while God’s wisdom helps us understand how to live out Christ in the midst of it. So don’t just keep analyzing and worrying with your own mind; return to God in prayer, take his word as your standard, and seek the Holy Spirit’s leading. The focus is not whether I can solve it, but whether Jesus can lead me; true faith is believing him even when we cannot yet see the answer.

Finally James lifts our eyes from the temporary to the eternal. Wealth, status, and outward success are all like the flower in the grass and will pass away; but those who love God and faithfully endure will receive “the crown of life.” So real victory in life is not never having trials, but still loving, trusting, and following the Lord in the midst of them. When we stop letting circumstances be king and let Jesus be King, God can use every trial to shape us, so that our lives grow more mature and more like Christ.
a: Change how you see trials
Look not only at the difficulty, but at the life God is shaping.
Ask God for wisdom
Don’t grit your teeth on your own; seek God’s word and the Holy Spirit’s guidance.
Endure to the end
Fix your eyes on eternity and don’t let temporary circumstances shake your faith.
q: What is God changing in my life through the trial I am facing now?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, when I fall into trials, help me see not only my circumstances but that You are shaping my life. Give me wisdom from You, so that I don’t rely on myself but look to Jesus in faith and follow the Holy Spirit’s leading. Help me endure to the end, grow more mature, and become more and more like Christ. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: The testing of my faith produces endurance, so that my life will be perfect and complete.

t: Trust God and Walk the Right Road
v: He who heeds the Word finds prosperity. Whoever trusts in the LORD is blessed.
The wise in heart shall be called prudent. Pleasantness of the lips promotes instruction.
Understanding is a fountain of life to one who has it, but the punishment of fools is their folly.
The heart of the wise instructs his mouth, and adds learning to his lips.
Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.
There is a way which seems right to a man, but in the end it leads to death.
b: Proverbs reminds us that the most dangerous thing in life is not “not knowing the road,” but being convinced that the road we are on must be right. Verse 25 says, “There is a way which seems right to a man, but in the end it leads to death.” Human judgment is limited, and our own feelings can deceive us. So true wisdom is not insisting on “what I think” in everything, but humbly laying down our own sovereignty, taking God’s word as our standard, and trusting the LORD, letting God guide us on the road we should take.

True wisdom also moves from the heart into the mouth. “The heart of the wise instructs his mouth” means that problems with our words often have their root in our life. If the heart is full of pride, bitterness, and self-centeredness, the mouth easily wounds people; if Christ reigns in the heart, filled with kindness, humility, and love, the words we speak can build people up. So it is not only about learning to “say good things” but first letting God change our heart; when life changes, daily living and relationships naturally change too.

“Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.” An encouraging word that comes from love can lift up the discouraged; a fitting word of comfort can become the strength that helps the wounded stand again. Let us not walk life’s road by our own cleverness, but trust God and seek the Holy Spirit’s guidance. And let us let Jesus be King in our hearts, so that our mouths become an outlet of life, building up and healing people with gracious words, and giving glory to God.
a: Rely on God in decisions
Don’t only ask, “How do I feel?” Ask, “What is God’s will?”
Manage the heart first, then the mouth
Let Christ change the inside first, and you can speak words that build people up.
Build people up with kind words
Encourage, comfort, and affirm more, so that people gain strength.
q: Is the road I am on now one that merely “seems right” to me, or am I truly seeking God’s will?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, give me humility and wisdom, so that I don’t rely on my own judgment but trust You and obey Your word. Holy Spirit, guide my heart so that Jesus is King in me, and guard my mouth so that I speak words that build up, comfort, and heal, and walk the road that pleases You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will trust in the LORD and be truly blessed.

t: God Sees, God Hears, and God Will Save
v: In the course of those many days, the king of Egypt died, and the children of Israel sighed because of the bondage, and they cried, and their cry came up to God because of the bondage.
God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.
God saw the children of Israel, and God understood.
The LORD said, “I have surely seen the affliction of my people who are in Egypt, and have heard their cry because of their taskmasters, for I know their sorrows.

I have come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them up out of that land to a good and large land, to a land flowing with milk and honey; to the place of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite.
Now, behold, the cry of the children of Israel has come to me. Moreover I have seen the oppression with which the Egyptians oppress them.
Come now therefore, and I will send you to Pharaoh, that you may bring my people, the children of Israel, out of Egypt.”
b: The Israelites suffered in Egypt for many years, as if God had been silent, yet Scripture uses several key words in a row: “God heard,” “God remembered,” “God saw,” “God was concerned.” God never forgot his people. And “remembered” does not mean God suddenly thought of them; it means he was about to act according to the covenant he had made. When we cannot see God at work in our suffering, we must not mistake his silence for his absence. He sees what we cannot see, hears what we cannot put into words, and fully knows the pain in our hearts.

God does more than know; he declares in person, “I have come down to deliver them.” The deliverance from Egypt foreshadows a more complete salvation: in Jesus Christ, God has come among us to set people free from the bondage of sin and bring them into true freedom and life. So when we are trapped in difficulty, our focus should not stay on ourselves, others, or circumstances, but turn to the Lord who delivers. The real way out is not to struggle out by ourselves, but to trust God’s grace and let him lead us on the road he has prepared.

Even more wonderful, God says, “I will send you to Pharaoh.” God heard his people’s cry, yet he chose Moses as the vessel of his rescue. It is the same today: when God lets us see someone else’s pain, he may be calling us to be an outlet of his love. True service is not forcing things by our own strength, nor building achievements for ourselves, but obeying God’s sending, relying on his power, and bringing people out of bondage and to Christ. God is the Savior and we are only vessels in his hands, so all the glory belongs to God.
a: Cry out to God in suffering
Believe that God sees, hears, and knows my pain.
Wait for God’s deliverance
Don’t grit your teeth on your own; fix your eyes on what God is doing.
Respond to God’s sending
When you see others’ needs, become a vessel through which God blesses them.
q: Do I believe that even when I can’t yet see any change, God still sees, hears, and is at work?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for seeing my situation, hearing my cry, and knowing the pain in my heart. When I cannot see a way out, help me keep trusting You, not struggling on my own but looking to Your salvation. Make me willing to answer Your sending and become a vessel in Your hands, bringing Your love and hope to those in need. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: God sees my affliction and hears my cry; he will surely come and deliver me himself.

t: Humility Brings True Unity
v: I therefore, the prisoner in the Lord, beg you to walk worthily of the calling with which you were called,
with all lowliness and humility, with patience, bearing with one another in love,
being eager to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
There is one body and one Spirit, even as you also were called in one hope of your calling,
one Lord, one faith, one baptism,
one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in us all.
b: Paul moves from the “grace received” of the first three chapters of Ephesians to the “daily life” of chapter four: since we have received God’s grace, our lives should be lived in a way that matches that grace. This is not putting on a show of godliness through outward rules, but letting the inner life be changed by Christ first, then flowing naturally into daily life and relationships. A truly mature life is not about proving how important I am, but about being humble, gentle, and patient like Jesus.

The greatest obstacle to unity is often not different opinions but each person’s insistence on himself. That is why Paul puts “lowliness” first. Humility doesn’t mean having no convictions; it means letting go of the heart that competes for power, victory, and face, and letting Jesus be Lord. We stop asking only “who is right” and are also willing to examine “what I need to change.” When we bear with one another in love, valuing people over issues and relationships over winning, the Holy Spirit can build real peace among us.

The church can be united not because everyone is the same, but because we share “one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God.” The center of unity is not any one person but Jesus Christ; and unity is not manufactured by human methods, but is “the unity of the Spirit,” which we are responsible to keep eagerly. When each of us turns our focus from ourselves to Jesus, submits to the Holy Spirit, and helps one another flourish, the different members can work together and become the glorious body of Christ.
a: Learn humility in everything
Insist on yourself less, and imitate Jesus more.
Bear with one another in love
Don’t hurt people over issues, or break relationships over winning.
Eagerly keep unity
Let Jesus be Lord, submit to the Holy Spirit, and help one another flourish.
q: In my current relationships, what do I need to lay down in order to humbly keep our unity?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for calling me in Christ. Help me live a life of humility, gentleness, and patience, bearing with others in love. Help me let go of myself and let Jesus be King in my heart, submit to the Holy Spirit’s leading, and eagerly keep the unity of heart, so that the body of Christ is built up and all the glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.

t: Resurrection Is in the Lord, and Life Is in the Lord
v: So when Jesus came, he found that he had been in the tomb four days already.
Now Bethany was near Jerusalem, about fifteen stadia away.
Many of the Jews had joined the women around Martha and Mary, to console them concerning their brother.
Then when Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went and met him, but Mary stayed in the house.
Therefore Martha said to Jesus, “Lord, if you would have been here, my brother wouldn’t have died.
Even now I know that whatever you ask of God, God will give you.”
Jesus said to her, “Your brother will rise again.”
Martha said to him, “I know that he will rise again in the resurrection at the last day.”
Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. He who believes in me will still live, even if he dies.
Whoever lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?”
She said to him, “Yes, Lord. I have come to believe that you are the Christ, God’s Son, he who comes into the world.”
b: When Jesus came to Bethany, Lazarus had already been dead four days. From a human point of view, it seemed that everything was too late. Martha said, “Lord, if you had been here…” When we are disappointed, we too often ask, “Lord, why didn’t you come sooner?” But God’s time is not our time. Where people see a tomb, Jesus sees resurrection; when we think things are over, God can still begin his new work. So don’t let circumstances decide your faith; turn your focus back to Jesus.

Jesus didn’t merely tell Martha that “there will be a resurrection someday.” He declared, “I am the resurrection and the life.” The center of the Christian faith is not just a doctrine about eternal life; it is Jesus himself. He doesn’t merely give us life; he himself is life. It is not that we overcome death by our own effort, but that Christ’s resurrection life enters into us. True life is no longer letting ourselves be in charge, but letting Jesus live in us and reign.

Finally Jesus asked Martha, “Do you believe this?” Faith in the end must move from “I know” to “I believe.” Martha went from believing the doctrine of the resurrection at the last day to declaring, “I have come to believe that you are the Christ, the Son of God.” True faith doesn’t wait to see a miracle before believing; it chooses to believe Jesus while the tomb is still there. When we move from our own point of view to God’s, we can see life in death and hope in despair, because the Lord we believe in is the resurrection and the life.
a: Don’t let circumstances settle things
The end of human ability can become the beginning of God’s work.
Focus on Jesus
True hope is not that circumstances change, but that the Lord of life is with us.
Move from knowing to believing
Choose to trust the Lord before you see the result.
q: Facing things in my life that seem “already too late,” do I still believe that Jesus is the resurrection and the life?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, when I face disappointment and circumstances that seem impossible, don’t let my eyes be limited by my situation, but fix them on Jesus. I believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, my resurrection and my life. May Jesus be King in me, so that in every situation I am filled with faith and hope. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Resurrection is in the Lord, and life is in the Lord; I trust in him and have eternal life.

t: Pray and Build at the Same Time
v: So we built the wall; and all the wall was joined together to half its height, for the people had a mind to work.

But when Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabians, the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites heard that the repairing of the walls of Jerusalem went forward, and that the breaches began to be filled, they were very angry;
and they all conspired together to come and fight against Jerusalem, and to cause confusion among us.
But we made our prayer to our God, and set a watch against them day and night because of them.
Judah said, “The strength of the bearers of burdens is fading and there is much rubble, so that we are not able to build the wall.”
Our adversaries said, “They will not know or see, until we come in among them and kill them, and cause the work to cease.”
When the Jews who lived by them came, they said to us ten times from all places, “Wherever you turn, they will attack us.”
Therefore I set guards in the lowest parts of the space behind the wall, in the open places. I set the people by family groups with their swords, their spears, and their bows.

I looked, and rose up, and said to the nobles, to the rulers, and to the rest of the people, “Don’t be afraid of them! Remember the Lord, who is great and awesome, and fight for your brothers, your sons, your daughters, your wives, and your houses.”
b: When the wall was half built, it was the easiest time to grow weary. There were enemy attacks from outside, voices inside saying “the strength… is fading,” and frightening news from every side. Yet Nehemiah didn’t let circumstances decide the direction. He brought the people’s focus back to God: “Don’t be afraid of them! Remember the Lord, who is great and awesome.” Fear makes us keep looking at how big the difficulty is; faith lets us see again how big God is. The harder the circumstances, the more we must turn our focus from ourselves, others, and circumstances to the Lord.

Nehemiah’s response was very practical: “We made our prayer to our God, and set a watch against them day and night.” He didn’t pray without acting, nor rely on human methods without praying. True faith first relies on God, and then faithfully does what we should do. Prayer acknowledges that power comes from God; keeping watch shows that people are faithful in their own rightful place. Let God be God and let people be people: not grasping God’s power, and not running from our own responsibility.

More importantly, the people did not fight separately; they stood together “by their families.” Nehemiah reminded them to fight for their brothers, children, wives, and homes. What God builds is never just an individual’s success but a people working together in unity to build God’s divine order. When each person lets go of self, lets God reign, and they watch over, work with, and build up one another, the breaches can be closed and the wall rebuilt. True victory is not “what I have accomplished,” but “God has accomplished his work through us.”
a: Remember the Lord when you are weary
Don’t keep looking at how big the difficulty is; look at how big God is.
Pray and act at the same time
Rely on God’s power, and faithfully do your own responsibility.
Watch over one another and build together
Don’t fight alone; work together in relationship and close the breaches.
q: Facing the breaches in my life, family, or ministry now, am I frightened by the difficulties, or am I remembering the Lord, praying, and rising up to build?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, when I am tired, afraid, and want to give up, help me remember again that You are great and awesome. Help me neither rely on myself nor run from responsibility, but depend on You in prayer and follow You faithfully in action. Help us watch over one another and build together in unity, closing the breaches in our lives, families, and church, letting Jesus be King, so that all the glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Don’t be afraid of them! Remember the Lord, who is great and awesome.

t: Do Not Worry; Seek God’s Kingdom First
v: Therefore I tell you, don’t be anxious for your life: what you will eat, or what you will drink; nor yet for your body, what you will wear. Isn’t life more than food, and the body more than clothing?
See the birds of the sky, that they don’t sow, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns. Your heavenly Father feeds them. Aren’t you of much more value than they?
“Which of you by being anxious, can add one moment to his lifespan?
Why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow. They don’t toil, neither do they spin,
yet I tell you that even Solomon in all his glory was not dressed like one of these.
But if God so clothes the grass of the field, which today exists and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, won’t he much more clothe you, you of little faith?
“Therefore don’t be anxious, saying, ‘What will we eat?’, ‘What will we drink?’ or, ‘With what will we be clothed?’
For the Gentiles seek after all these things; for your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things.
But seek first God’s Kingdom and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.
Therefore don’t be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Each day’s own evil is sufficient.
b: Jesus says “do not worry” three times. He is not telling us to be irresponsible, but not to let a tomorrow that has not yet come steal the peace God gives us today. The birds are fed and the lilies are clothed; how much more are we, the beloved children of our heavenly Father? Jesus says, “Your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things.” Before we even open our mouths, the Father already knows. Worry keeps our focus on “what do I do?”; faith turns our focus to “my Father knows.”

Jesus doesn’t only tell us “do not worry”; he also tells us where to set our hearts: “seek first God’s Kingdom, and his righteousness.” The real problem in life is often not that there is too much to do but that the order is wrong. When we are king, we want to control everything; when Jesus is King, we hand sovereignty back to God. To seek God’s Kingdom first is to ask first “what does God want?” and not only “what do I want?”; to let God’s will be accomplished in me first, and then to display his Kingdom through my life.

So the key to overcoming worry is not grasping tomorrow but trusting the God who reigns today. Jesus says, “Each day’s own evil is sufficient.” Tomorrow is in God’s hands; today is what God has given us. Hand over what we cannot control, and faithfully do what we should do today; take the Bible as our standard, seek the Holy Spirit’s guidance, and follow the life of Jesus. When our focus is on Jesus, not on ourselves, others, or circumstances, our hearts can return from worry to trust, and from grasping control to rest.
a: Hand your worries to the Father
He knows my needs and will surely care for me.
Put God’s Kingdom first
Seek God’s will in everything and let Jesus be King.
Live today well
Don’t borrow tomorrow’s worries; faithfully do today’s tasks.
q: What worries me most right now? Am I willing to hand sovereignty to God and seek his Kingdom and his righteousness first?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for knowing my needs and always caring for me. Help me let go of my worry about tomorrow and stop trying to control everything by myself, but let Jesus be King in my life. Help me each day to seek Your Kingdom and Your righteousness first, to live today faithfully, and to trust that tomorrow is still in Your hands. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: “Seek first God’s Kingdom, and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.”

t: God Asks You, “Where Are You?”
v: They heard the LORD God’s voice walking in the garden in the cool of the day, and the man and his wife hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God among the trees of the garden.
The LORD God called to the man, and said to him, “Where are you?”
The man said, “I heard your voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; so I hid myself.”
God said, “Who told you that you were naked? Have you eaten from the tree that I commanded you not to eat from?”
The man said, “The woman whom you gave to be with me, she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate it.”
The LORD God said to the woman, “What have you done?” The woman said, “The serpent deceived me, and I ate.”

The LORD God said to the serpent, “Because you have done this, you are cursed above all livestock, and above every animal of the field. You shall go on your belly and you shall eat dust all the days of your life.
I will put hostility between you and the woman, and between your offspring and her offspring. He will bruise your head, and you will bruise his heel.”
b: The first reaction of humanity after sin was to “hide.” Adam, who had walked closely with God, now hid from God in fear and shame; and when God questioned him, he shifted the blame to Eve, and Eve shifted it to the serpent. Sin turns people from “being with God” to “hiding from God,” and from “seeing ourselves” to “blaming others.” So God asked, “Where are you?” Not because God didn’t know where Adam was, but because God wanted Adam to see the true condition of his life. The starting point of life change is to stop hiding, stop shifting blame, and honestly return to God and see our problem.

Yet in the darkest moment of the fall, God had already declared the hope of salvation. Genesis 3:15 says, “He will bruise your head, and you will bruise his heel.” Christians through the ages have called this verse the “Protoevangelium” (the first gospel), because it points ahead to God’s final victory over sin and Satan through Christ. Man sinned and left God, but God took the initiative to seek man; man failed, but God prepared salvation. The gospel is not people working hard to climb back to God, but God coming in Christ to seek and save the lost.

So victory does not come from the old self trying harder, but from letting Christ’s new life reign in us. The root of sin is that people leave their rightful place and want to decide good and evil and rule for themselves; salvation brings us back to the right place, letting people be people and God be God. When we stop hiding, stop blaming others, humbly admit our need of grace, and let Jesus be King, we can move from self-centeredness to selflessness, and from failure into Christ’s victory. Change begins with me, and what truly changes me is God’s grace in Christ.
a: Stop hiding
Honestly face your real condition before God.
Stop blaming
Don’t look only at others’ problems; first see what you need to change.
Come back to Jesus
Don’t overcome sin by your own effort; let Christ reign in your life.
q: When God asks me today, “Where are you?”, what in my life am I hiding from God and unwilling to face?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, shine Your light on me, so that I stop hiding and stop shifting responsibility to others, and humbly see my own problems. Thank You for still seeking people after they sinned and for preparing salvation in Jesus Christ. Bring me back into Your presence, help me lay down my own sovereignty, and let Jesus be King in me, so that I live out the victorious new life of Christ. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: “He will bruise your head, and you will bruise his heel.”

t: Real Love Must Be Lived Out
v: My little children, let’s not love in word only, or with the tongue only, but in deed and truth.
And by this we know that we are of the truth and persuade our hearts before him,
because if our heart condemns us, God is greater than our heart, and knows all things.
Beloved, if our hearts don’t condemn us, we have boldness toward God;
so whatever we ask, we receive from him, because we keep his commandments and do the things that are pleasing in his sight.
This is his commandment, that we should believe in the name of his Son, Jesus Christ, and love one another, even as he commanded.
He who keeps his commandments remains in him, and he in him. By this we know that he remains in us, by the Spirit which he gave us.
b: John brings love from “saying” to “living”: “not in word only, neither with the tongue only, but in deed and truth.” True love is not just the words “I love you”; it is being willing to give when the other is in need, to forgive when hurt, and to lay oneself down first in conflict. Jesus is the most perfect example: he didn’t just tell us he loves us; on the cross he gave himself up and truly lived out that love. So a changed life must bring changed relationships; when Christ’s love enters us, it will surely flow from our lives to others.

But sometimes our own weakness makes us condemn ourselves, even doubting whether we are worthy to come before God. John comforts us: “God is greater than our heart.” Our feelings are not the final judge; God is. He fully knows our failures, and fully knows the grace we have received in Christ. So don’t keep being condemned by your feelings; turn your focus back to Jesus. When we come honestly before God and receive his light, forgiveness, and renewal, our hearts can be at rest again and come boldly before him.

In the end John boils the Christian life down to two things: “believe in Jesus” and “love one another.” Faith unites us with Christ, and love lets Christ’s life flow out of us. And this isn’t something we force ourselves to do, because God has given us the Holy Spirit. A true Christian life is led by the Holy Spirit, with Jesus reigning within, turning us from “caring only for ourselves” to loving God and people. Life first, then relationships; when Christ’s life fills us, love is no longer just a word but becomes a visible way of living.
a: Turn love into action
Today, take the initiative to do one practical thing that shows love to someone.
Don’t be ruled by self-condemnation
Receive God’s light, and believe that God’s grace is greater than your feelings.
Let the Holy Spirit live out Christ’s love
Don’t force yourself to love; let Jesus be King within.
q: Who in my family, church, or relationships today needs me to turn “love in my mouth” into “practical action”?
Who in my family, church, or relationships today needs me to turn “love in my mouth” into “practical action”?
pr:
Dear heavenly Father, thank You for showing me true love in Jesus Christ. Help me not only say I love, but truly love people in daily life. When my heart condemns me, help me remember that You are greater than my heart; fill me with the Holy Spirit, let Jesus be King in me, and let Christ’s love flow from my life to everyone around me. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

When my heart condemns me, help me remember that You are greater than my heart; fill me with the Holy Spirit, let Jesus be King in me, and let Christ’s love flow from my life to everyone around me.
